glance_notes.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Election Dates
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadlines: For Louisiana's November 3, 2026 election, the deadline to register in person, by mail or through an Office of Motor Vehicles office is October 5. The deadline to register through the GeauxVote Online Registration System is October 13.

glance_notes.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Election Dates
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 20–27: Early voting for the November 3, 2026 election runs October 20 through October 27, excluding Sunday, October 25. Early voting hours are 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

glance_notes.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Voting in Louisiana
glance_notes.text: Absentee Voting by Mail Requires Eligibility: Louisiana does not provide unrestricted no-excuse absentee voting by mail. A voter generally must qualify under one of the reasons established by state law. For the November 3, 2026 election, the ordinary absentee-ballot request deadline is October 30 at 4:30 p.m.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Louisiana residents may register online through the GeauxVote Online Registration System, in person at a Registrar of Voters office, by mail, or through designated agencies including Office of Motor Vehicles locations. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 17 years old to register and at least 18 years old to vote, and establish Louisiana residence. A person under an order of imprisonment for a felony conviction may register and vote only if the person meets Louisiana's statutory eligibility requirements for restoration of voting rights. A person under a judgment of full interdiction for mental incompetence or partial interdiction with suspension of voting rights is not eligible to register unless the applicable court order restores that right.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, Registrar of Voters or designated agency
register.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Louisiana's registration rules contain important qualifications concerning felony convictions and interdiction. The Secretary of State's official registration materials should control rather than a simplified permanent-disenfranchisement description. Louisiana permits registration at age 16 in limited circumstances when registering in person at a Registrar of Voters office or Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles, while general registration eligibility begins at 17. The reader-facing text uses the broadly applicable age rule rather than overcomplicating the main description.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Louisiana Voter Portal or GeauxVote mobile app to check your voter registration information. The voter portal also provides polling-place information, sample ballots, election dates, voting districts, absentee-ballot information and other personalized election information.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the Louisiana Voter Portal
check_registration.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Louisiana Voter Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State repeatedly directs voters to the Louisiana Voter Portal for registration status and personalized voting information. The GeauxVote app provides access to the same voter-focused election information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 election, the deadline to register in person, by mail or through an Office of Motor Vehicles office is October 5. A mailed application must satisfy Louisiana's applicable postmark deadline. Voters using the GeauxVote Online Registration System have until October 13. Louisiana does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Election Dates
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State's 2026 election information directly establishes October 5 for in-person, mail and OMV registration and October 13 for GeauxVote online registration. Louisiana's voter-registration FAQ at [https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/voter-registration-faqs](https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/voter-registration-faqs) explains the underlying rule: registration must generally occur at least 30 days before the election for in-person or mail registration and at least 20 days before the election through GeauxVote online registration.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Louisiana voters can use the Louisiana Voter Portal or GeauxVote mobile app to find their Election Day polling location. Because polling places and precinct assignments can change, voters should verify their location before each election. Election Day voters generally vote at the polling place assigned to their precinct.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place in the Voter Portal
polling_place.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Louisiana Voter Portal
polling_place.internal_note: The Louisiana Voter Portal is the Secretary of State's official personalized voter-information service and provides polling-place information based on the voter's registration record.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Louisiana's next statewide federal election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Because this is a regularly scheduled congressional election, polls are open from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Voters casting a ballot in person are asked to present accepted identification. A voter without photo identification may still vote by completing and signing a voter identification affidavit and providing the additional information required by Louisiana law.
election_day.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Election Dates
election_day.internal_note: Louisiana R.S. 18:541 establishes a normal 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. schedule but specifically requires 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for regularly scheduled congressional primary elections and elections held at the same time. The Secretary of State's 2026 election page expressly confirms 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for November 3, 2026. This distinction is important because Louisiana's December 12, 2026 election uses 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. hours.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: For the November 3, 2026 election, Louisiana polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Louisiana's standard hours for many other primary and general elections are 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., but regularly scheduled congressional elections use the earlier 6:00 a.m. opening time.
polling_hours.internal_note: R.S. 18:541(A) sets ordinary primary/general polling hours at 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Subsection B provides that regularly scheduled congressional primary elections and elections held at the same time open at 6:00 a.m. The Secretary of State election-dates page independently confirms the 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. schedule for November 3, 2026.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Any registered Louisiana voter may vote early in person without providing a reason. For the November 3, 2026 election, early voting is October 20 through October 27, excluding Sunday, October 25. Early voting locations are open from 8:30 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. during the scheduled early-voting days. Voters should check the Louisiana Voter Portal or their Registrar of Voters for the appropriate early-voting location.
early_voting.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Voting in Louisiana
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes October 20-27, excluding Sunday October 25, and 8:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. hours for the November 3 election. Early voting is available without the eligibility restrictions that apply to voting absentee by mail. Exact locations can be obtained through the Voter Portal and Registrar of Voters offices.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Louisiana generally requires a voter to meet an eligible reason to vote absentee by mail. Qualifying categories include voters age 65 or older, voters with disabilities, military and overseas voters, certain students and higher-education personnel living outside their parish of registration, voters temporarily absent during early voting and Election Day, certain clergy, offshore workers, hospitalized voters, sequestered jurors and several other circumstances established by state law. For the November 3, 2026 election, ordinary absentee-ballot requests must be received by 4:30 p.m. on October 30. The Registrar of Voters must receive an ordinary completed absentee ballot by 4:30 p.m. on November 2. Different deadlines apply to military and overseas voters.
absentee_mail.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Voting in Louisiana
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current absentee FAQ at [https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/absentee-voting-faqs](https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/absentee-voting-faqs) provides the complete qualifying-reason list and also identifies special first-time-voter restrictions for some voters who registered online or by mail. The official election-dates page establishes October 30 at 4:30 p.m. as the ordinary request deadline and November 2 at 4:30 p.m. as the ordinary receipt deadline for the November 3 election. Military and overseas voters have separate deadlines documented in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Louisiana voters appearing to vote in person are asked to identify themselves with an accepted photo ID. Accepted identification includes a Louisiana driver's license, Louisiana special identification card, a U.S. military identification card containing the voter's name and picture, or another generally recognized picture identification card containing the voter's name and signature. A voter who does not have an accepted photo ID may still vote by signing a voter identification affidavit and providing the additional identifying information required by law.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID requested; affidavit option available
voter_id.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Voting in Louisiana
voter_id.internal_note: The Secretary of State's early-voting guidance directly identifies Louisiana driver's licenses, Louisiana special ID cards, U.S. military identification containing name and picture, and other generally recognized picture IDs containing name and signature. Louisiana's system is not accurately described as an absolute photo-ID requirement because state law provides an affidavit procedure for voters without photo identification.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Louisiana provides voting assistance and accessible options for voters with disabilities. Voters who need assistance may receive help with voting as allowed by state and federal law. A voter with a qualifying disability may be eligible for absentee voting by mail and, in appropriate circumstances, may qualify for ongoing absentee-ballot status. Louisiana also operates a Nursing Home Early Voting Program for eligible residents of nursing facilities. Voters needing accommodations should contact their parish Registrar of Voters before voting to confirm the available assistance and accessibility arrangements.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Assistance, absentee options and nursing-home voting available
accessible_voting.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Disabled and Elderly Citizens
accessible_voting.internal_note: Louisiana maintains dedicated voting procedures for disabled and elderly voters, including disability-based absentee voting and the Nursing Home Early Voting Program. The Secretary of State's ways-to-vote page at [https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/ways-to-vote](https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/ways-to-vote) also provides the specialized Disabled Application and Nursing Home Early Voting Program application. Specific assistance requirements can depend on the voter's circumstances, so parish Registrar of Voters offices are the appropriate local contacts.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Louisiana provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying dependents and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may register or update their registration online or by submitting an application to their parish Registrar of Voters. They may also use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot at the same time. Ballots may be requested for delivery by mail, fax or email, and the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot may be used for federal offices by eligible voters who have registered and requested an absentee ballot. For the November 3, 2026 election, military and overseas absentee-ballot requests must be received by 4:30 p.m. Central Time on November 2. Voted ballots from military personnel and U.S. citizens residing outside the United States must be received by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery and FWAB available
military_overseas.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: The current Secretary of State military/overseas page directly establishes FPCA use, electronic ballot delivery, FWAB eligibility for federal offices, the 4:30 p.m. Central Time day-before-election request deadline and the 8:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline for military personnel and U.S. citizens residing outside the United States. It also confirms Louisiana's 30-day standard registration deadline and 20-day GeauxVote online deadline for these voters.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may register in Louisiana if the student establishes Louisiana residence and otherwise meets the state's voter qualifications. A registered voter who is a student, instructor or professor living outside the parish where the person is registered, or the qualifying spouse or dependent of that person, may be eligible to vote absentee by mail. Louisiana voters should maintain only one legal voting residence and should update their registration when their residence changes.
student_voting.glance_value: Students away from their parish may qualify for absentee voting
student_voting.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Voting in Louisiana
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's absentee guidance specifically identifies higher-education students, instructors and professors located and living outside their parish of registration, along with qualifying spouses and dependents, as eligible to apply for absentee voting. The absentee FAQ at [https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/absentee-voting-faqs](https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/absentee-voting-faqs) also identifies a student-ID or fee-bill exception to Louisiana's first-time absentee-voter restriction. The section does not imply that attending a Louisiana college automatically establishes Louisiana voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Louisiana voters can view personalized sample ballots through the Louisiana Voter Portal and GeauxVote mobile app. Online sample ballots are made available no later than 20 days before each election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's precinct and electoral districts, voters should use their own registration information to view the ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Available no later than 20 days before the election
sample_ballot.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Ballot Numbers and Sample Ballots
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that sample ballots are available no later than 20 days before each election and notes that online sample ballots do not contain withdrawn candidates. Personalized ballot information is available through the Louisiana Voter Portal at [https://voterportal.sos.la.gov/](https://voterportal.sos.la.gov/).

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Louisiana Secretary of State, GeauxVote Elections Division, 8585 Archives Avenue, Baton Rouge, LA 70809. Elections Division phone: 800-883-2805 or 225-922-0900. Fax: 225-922-0945. Elections Services phone: 225-922-0900. For questions about an individual voter registration, absentee ballot, early-voting location or other local voting matter, contact the parish Registrar of Voters.
contact.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The current Secretary of State contact page directly verifies the Elections Division at 8585 Archives Ave., 800-883-2805, 225-922-0900 and fax 225-922-0945. Elections Services is also listed at 8585 Archives Ave. with 225-922-0900. No unverified email address is inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Louisiana Secretary of State Elections and Voting website for statewide election information, registration rules, election dates, absentee voting, early voting, military and overseas voting and accessibility resources. The Louisiana Voter Portal provides personalized registration information, polling locations, sample ballots and absentee-ballot information. Parish Registrars of Voters administer voter registration and many voter services locally.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, Voter Portal & parish registrars
official_resources.source_name: Louisiana Secretary of State — Elections & Voting
official_resources.internal_note: Official election dates: [https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/election-dates](https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/election-dates).
